body:

Notice in the chart how the weak options drop to zero while the kept options grow taller.

title: Top-k filtering and reported probabilities
body:
When a language model samples text, it often applies top-k filtering to restrict choices to the top $k$ most likely tokens.

This mechanism strips out all tokens outside the top $k$ set and renormalizes the remaining probabilities so they sum to one.

```rh-diagram

```

Looking at the bar chart, the full softmax assigns original probabilities that sum to $100\%$ across all options. Once the lowest token is dropped, the surviving probabilities are scaled up by dividing by the kept share.

As a result, the reported probability of any chosen token within the top $k$ increases after renormalization.

This shift means logged probabilities from top-k filtered models no longer reflect the true underlying softmax distribution.

When a language model generates text, it computes raw scores called logits for every token in its vocabulary. These logits are converted into probabilities via the softmax function, which ensures all values sum to one.

Top-k filtering removes all tokens except the $k$ highest-probability candidates. The remaining probabilities are then rescaled to sum to one, a process known as renormalization.

Because the denominator shrinks when low-probability tokens are discarded, the relative probabilities of the kept tokens increase.

Consequently, the reported probability of the chosen token changes after filtering is applied.
